ch05.n.d.force: How long the force acts on the puck: the first 2 s only, or all the time
ch05.n.d.strobe: Marks the puck position on the track every 0.5 s
ch05.n.goal.first: First law: with zero net force the velocity is constant (at rest or uniform straight-line motion)
ch05.n.goal.second: Second law: acceleration $a = F_\text{net}/m$, proportional to the force and inversely proportional to the mass
ch05.n.obs.off: Removed after 2 s: once the force is gone, $a = 0$ and $v$ stays the same, so the puck does not stop
ch05.n.obs.mass: Twice the mass: half the acceleration for the same force, half the slope of $v(t)$
ch05.n.obs.strobe: Strobe: the spacing grows while the force acts and is constant after it is removed
ch05.n.assume: Frictionless horizontal surface, constant horizontal force
ch05.t.d.mA: Mass $m_A$ of the left cart A
ch05.t.d.mB: Mass $m_B$ of the right cart B
ch05.t.d.F: Size $F$ of the force with which the carts push each other (for 1 s)
ch05.t.goal.pair: Third law: the force of A on B and the force of B on A have equal size and opposite directions
ch05.t.goal.mass: Equal forces, so the accelerations are inversely proportional to the masses
ch05.t.obs.mirror: $F(t)$: the force on A (solid) and the force on B (dashed) are mirror images about zero
ch05.t.obs.ratio: $m_A = 1$ kg, $m_B = 2$ kg: $\lvert a_A\rvert$ is twice $\lvert a_B\rvert$
ch05.t.obs.equal: Whatever the masses, the two forces have the same size; changing a mass leaves $F(t)$ unchanged
ch05.t.obs.after: After they separate: zero force, both carts move uniformly
ch05.t.assume: Frictionless horizontal track, constant push during the 1 s of contact
ch05.f.d.frame: View from the ground, or move along with the train
ch05.f.d.motion: Motion of the train relative to the ground: uniform (2 m/s) or accelerating
ch05.f.d.A: Acceleration $a_0$ of the train relative to the ground
ch05.f.d.pseudo: In the accelerating train, show the pseudo force $-m\vec a_0$ on the ball (dashed)
ch05.f.goal.inertial: Inertial frame: a frame in which the first law holds. A frame moving uniformly relative to an inertial frame is inertial too
ch05.f.goal.non: Accelerating frame: objects accelerate with no force on them, the first law fails, so the frame is non-inertial
ch05.f.obs.ground: Ground frame: the ball keeps its initial velocity; it is the train that accelerates
ch05.f.obs.uniform: Uniform train: in the train frame the ball stays at rest on the table, $a = 0$, the same laws as on the ground
ch05.f.obs.accel: Accelerating train, train frame: zero horizontal force on the ball, yet it accelerates backwards, $a = -a_0$
ch05.f.obs.pseudo: Pseudo force $-m\vec a_0$: not exerted by any other body; it is added so that the second law keeps its form in a non-inertial frame
ch05.f.assume: Frictionless table, ball mass 1 kg, the ball initially moves with the train at 2 m/s
